narrative.overview: VisualRefiner treats every file as material placed on a real inspection surface. The system borrows from proofing tables, registration marks, crop rulers, contact sheets, and optical inspection tools. It is light, materially layered, deliberately asymmetrical, and led by working product proof rather than marketing chrome.
keyCharacteristics: Pale celadon work surfaces with warm inspection paper.
Calibration orange appears only on actions and directional emphasis.
Large compact display type faces working media surfaces.
Registration geometry is functional, sparse, and tied to file inspection.

rules.name: The Action Signal Rule
rules.body: Calibration orange identifies actions or movement; it does not decorate passive copy or large background fields.

rules.name: The Two-Tone Focus Rule
rules.body: Keyboard focus uses a graphite outline with a signal-yellow separation ring so it remains visible on paper and celadon.

rules.name: The One Dominant Statement Rule
rules.body: Each surface receives one oversized typographic statement. Controls and section headings step down clearly instead of competing with it.

rules.name: The Flat Bench Rule
rules.body: Ordinary rows and containers stay flat. Shadows belong only to movable or pressable objects.

dos: Do place a real file action or working tool in the first viewport.
Do reserve calibration orange for actions, active controls, and directional signals.
Do use ledger rows and asymmetric splits for multi-tool navigation.
Do let privacy claims point to a visible local-processing mechanism.
Do keep mobile tasks vertically continuous and touch targets at least 46px high.
donts: Don't introduce blue-purple gradients, neon AI-editor styling, or generic SaaS card walls.
Don't use an eyebrow above a major heading.
Don't use emoji or Unicode glyphs as interface icons; use Iconify or authored geometry.
Don't decorate passive surfaces with calibration orange.
Don't apply measurement grids outside genuine file workspaces.
Don't add ambient shadows to every container or combine wide shadows with decorative borders.
